[page[title]]

Every method chained from an invocation result must begin on a new line.

What The Standard says

“Abstraction” — The Standard's canonical fluent registrations and invocations put each continuation on its own line, making the sequence easy to scan. read it here.
“exposure control” — The Standard values a small, understandable surface. Vertically aligning chained calls keeps each operation visible instead of hiding behavior across a long line. read it here.

Why it matters

Putting each stage of a fluent chain on its own line reveals order and transformation as a readable pipeline. It also makes additions, removals, breakpoints, and code review diffs local to the affected stage.

Bad code example

// Violates STXFORMAT009: Every method chained from an invocation result must begin on a new line.
students.Where(student => student.IsReady).ToArray();

Good code example

// Follows STXFORMAT009
students
    .Where(student => student.IsReady)
    .ToArray();
